newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK foreign reserves nearly US$70 bln -- HKMA's Yam.
newsitem.headline: HK foreign reserves nearly US$70 bln -- HKMA's Yam.

text.p: Hong Kong's foreign reserves stand at nearly US$70 billion, the seventh largest in the world, said chief executive Joseph Yam of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), the territory's defacto central bank.
The sum represents about six times the amount of currency in circulation, Yam said in an article published in the South China Morning Post on Monday.
Last month, the HKMA announced foreign reserves of US$63.8 billion at the end of 1996, and US$69.6 billion if forward transactions to be settled were included.
"Without being complacent, we feel technically in a rather comfortable position if ever there were a need to defend our exchange rate against speculative attacks," Yam said.
The local curreny has in recent days been weak against the U.S. dollar, trading at about HK$7.7490 to US$1.00, hit by renewed concerns about the health of Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
The exchange rate, pegged at HK$7.80 to US$1.00, has tended to trade between HK$7.73 and HK$7.74 in recent years.
